name: International Protection (Asylum)

qualifying_event.description: A person physically present in Sweden with a well-founded fear of persecution, or facing death, corporal punishment, torture, or serious harm from armed conflict, may apply for refugee status or subsidiary protection.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Application at a border control point or a Migration Agency Reception and Return Centre (Malmo, Gothenburg, Stockholm, or Boden); identity documents; interview.

requirements.blocker_text: Well-founded fear of persecution due to race, nationality, religion, political views, gender, sexual orientation, or social group membership, where national authorities cannot or will not protect the applicant.
Facing death, corporal punishment, torture, inhumane or degrading treatment, or serious injury as a civilian from armed conflict.

evidence_required.document: Supporting evidence for the protection claim

outcome.duration_length: Refugee status: 3-year permit (renewable); Subsidiary protection: 13-month permit (renewable)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Sweden). MAJOR RECENT REFORM, worth flagging prominently and distinctly from se_permanent_residence.json's general notes: as of 12 July 2026, Sweden stopped granting new PERMANENT residence permits to refugees, subsidiary-protection holders, quota (resettled) refugees, exceptionally-distressing-circumstances grantees, long-term-resident-status holders, and certain enforcement-obstacle cases -- previously, these categories eventually converted their initial permit (3 years for refugees, 13 months for subsidiary protection, as still modeled in this file's outcome) into a PERMANENT residence permit after a further qualifying period. Now, at that same conversion point, they instead receive a renewable 5-YEAR temporary permit (not modeled as a separate route here since it functions as a straightforward renewal of the same underlying protection status, not a new application). leads_to_pr is modeled FALSE specifically because of this reform -- a genuine, very recent change from how this route worked before. Citizenship remains reachable WITHOUT ever holding a permanent residence permit: the exemption rules let a refugee/subsidiary-protection holder apply for naturalization if they can show 'well-founded prospects' their permit will keep being renewed, or automatically once they hit 10 years' Swedish residence regardless of that prospects test -- citizenship_after_months (84) reflects the refugee-specific 7-year naturalization residence bar under se_naturalisation.json's refugee group, the most directly applicable figure. Existing permanent residence permits granted before 12 July 2026 are unaffected and not withdrawn by this reform.
